failure_summary.description: Agents imported injected tools from a nonexistent `tools` module despite the skill’s direct-call instruction.
Agents skipped a needed cached-result update, used unfiltered inputs for a nearest search, or repeated criteria already reflected in the cached result.
A missing flight and hotel date led the agent to omit an independent restaurant search whose required inputs were known.
A round-trip request omitted the return-leg search and did not encode the explicit non-stop constraint.
A one-sided time cutoff was encoded in 24-hour format rather than as an AM/PM time range.

patch.reasoning: The repeated import and general cache/independent-search failures are already explicitly addressed by the skill, so duplicating those instructions is unwarranted. These edits clarify uncovered parameter mapping for non-stop flights and one-sided time bounds, and specify that newly filtered inputs must be used for downstream proximity searches.

edits.target: - Preserve user-provided dates, entity values, and casing. For a round trip, make two separate flight searches: one outbound and one with the route reversed for the return. Use each leg’s date as its `departure_date`; do not represent the return leg by setting `arrival_date` on the outbound search. Ask for an unknown endpoint rather than assuming a route. When a hotel stay is given as a check-in date plus an unambiguous duration in nights rather than a checkout date, call `adjust_date(date=<check-in date>, delta_days=<number of nights>)` and use its returned date as checkout; do not treat the duration as missing.
edits.content: - Preserve user-provided dates, entity values, and casing. For a round trip, make two separate flight searches: one outbound and one with the route reversed for the return. Use each leg’s date as its `departure_date`; do not represent the return leg by setting `arrival_date` on the outbound search. Encode an explicit non-stop or direct request as `num_layovers=[0]` on each applicable leg. Ask for an unknown endpoint rather than assuming a route. When a hotel stay is given as a check-in date plus an unambiguous duration in nights rather than a checkout date, call `adjust_date(date=<check-in date>, delta_days=<number of nights>)` and use its returned date as checkout; do not treat the duration as missing.

edits.target: - Match arguments only to fields declared by the selected tool’s schema, with the expected type and cardinality. Never pass a preference as an unsupported extra argument or place it in an unrelated field. For range-shaped fields, encode an explicitly exact value as both endpoints (for example, `[n, n]`); encode a minimum rating or a request for at least or better as `[n, schema_max]`. Treat stated soft preferences as actionable: translate a standard time-of-day preference without exact bounds into a reasonable interval in the expected format (for example, afternoon as `12:00 PM`–`5:00 PM`). For attraction searches, use each explicitly provided location field (`city` and/or `state`) in the matching schema field along with the requested category or name. A state alone is usable when the tool supports state-level search; do not ask for a city when it does.
edits.content: - Match arguments only to fields declared by the selected tool’s schema, with the expected type and cardinality. Never pass a preference as an unsupported extra argument or place it in an unrelated field. For range-shaped fields, encode an explicitly exact value as both endpoints (for example, `[n, n]`); encode a minimum rating or a request for at least or better as `[n, schema_max]`. Treat stated soft preferences as actionable: translate a standard time-of-day preference without exact bounds into a reasonable interval in the expected format (for example, afternoon as `12:00 PM`–`5:00 PM`). For time-range arguments, use AM/PM strings; when the only stated bound is “by” a time or “as early as possible,” use midnight through that bound. For attraction searches, use each explicitly provided location field (`city` and/or `state`) in the matching schema field along with the requested category or name. A state alone is usable when the tool supports state-level search; do not ask for a city when it does.

edits.target: - For recommendations near another result type, ensure compatible results for both types are available, then call `search_nearest` and save its result. Set `groupBy` to the domain the user wants as the organizing base; when lodging is the planned base, group by hotel.
edits.content: - For recommendations near another result type, ensure compatible results for both types are available. If the user has added criteria for either input, filter and save that input before calling `search_nearest`, and pass the updated result rather than its stale cached version; save the nearest result too. Set `groupBy` to the domain the user wants as the organizing base; when lodging is the planned base, group by hotel.
